answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use a reputation inlet: every new identity enters through a slow, work-gated channel and must complete small verifiable tasks before transacting at full volume. Each completed task emits a public signal, a signed record of useful work, and peers weight that signal by age and cost. A saffron marker, a small refundable bond posted at entry, is slashed if the identity spams or duplicates work. Faking thousands of identities then costs thousands of bonds plus thousands of hours of real work, while one honest agent pays once and reuses its reputation forever.
